stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-5.4 with native computer use, 1M-token context, and record benchmarks
key_facts: OpenAI released GPT-5.4 on March 5 in three configurations: standard, Thinking (for ChatGPT Plus/Team/Pro), and Pro (for ChatGPT Pro and Enterprise), also available via API and Codex
On GDPval, a benchmark assessing knowledge work across 44 professions in nine industries, GPT-5.4 matches or exceeds human professionals in 83% of comparisons, up from 70.9% for GPT-5.2
On OSWorld-Verified desktop navigation benchmark, GPT-5.4 scores 75% success rate versus 72.4% human benchmark and GPT-5.2's 47.3%
API supports up to 1 million tokens context window, double GPT-5.3's 400,000 tokens, with premium pricing at 2x rate after 272,000 tokens
Introduces native computer use for software operation and file navigation, and a reworked tool-calling system with Tool Search that reduces token usage 47% on large agent systems
Hallucinations reduced by 33% fewer incorrect factual claims and 18% fewer overall errors versus GPT-5.2
OpenAI published a new Chain-of-Thought Controllability evaluation finding GPT-5.4 Thinking shows low ability to obscure its reasoning, suggesting CoT monitoring remains a useful safety tool
Release comes just two days after GPT-5.3 Instant and amid user cancellations over OpenAI's Pentagon contract

stories.headline: Claude Opus 4.6 finds 22 Firefox security vulnerabilities in two weeks, 14 high-severity
key_facts: Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 discovered 22 security vulnerabilities in Firefox during a two-week test in January 2026, with 14 classified as high-severity by Mozilla
Claude found its first vulnerability — a Use After Free flaw in Firefox's JavaScript engine — within 20 minutes of initial exploration
Anthropic scanned nearly 6,000 C++ files and submitted 112 unique reports to Mozilla's Bugzilla tracker, including roughly 90 non-security bugs like crashes and logic errors
The 14 high-severity bugs represent nearly one-fifth of all high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities remediated throughout 2025
All vulnerabilities were patched in Firefox 148.0, which rolled out to hundreds of millions of users
Anthropic spent approximately $4,000 in API credits attempting to generate proof-of-concept exploits, succeeding in only 2 cases that required sandbox removal to function
Anthropic also announced Claude Code Security, an automated vulnerability-discovery and patching tool in limited research preview for Enterprise and Team customers
Anthropic reported finding over 500 previously unknown vulnerabilities across open-source projects during broader Opus 4.6 testing

stories.headline: Cursor launches Automations: event-driven AI agents that run without developer prompts
key_facts: Cursor launched Automations on March 4, enabling always-on AI agents triggered by external events — Slack messages, GitHub pull requests, PagerDuty alerts, or scheduled timers
The system replaces the manual prompt-and-response model with a conveyor belt of digital triggers that activate coding agents without human initiation
Cursor's annualized revenue surpassed $2 billion in February 2026, doubling from $1 billion in November 2025
Enterprise customers now account for 60% of revenue, with Nvidia and Stripe deploying Cursor across thousands of engineers
Cursor is valued at $29.3 billion following a $2.3 billion funding round in late 2025
Use cases include automated code review, security scanning, incident response, bug triage, and weekly change summaries
Cursor positions Automations as the 'Third Era' of AI development — beyond autocomplete and chat toward continuous autonomous agent operation

stories.headline: Luma launches creative AI agents on Uni-1 model for end-to-end multimodal production
key_facts: Luma AI launched Luma Agents on March 5, built on its new Uni-1 model — a decoder-only autoregressive transformer trained on audio, video, image, language, and spatial reasoning
Agents handle end-to-end creative workflows from brief to final delivery across text, image, video, and audio, coordinating multiple external models
Integrates with 8+ external models including Luma's Ray 3.14, Google Veo 3, ByteDance Seedream, and ElevenLabs voice models
Launch partners include Publicis Groupe, Serviceplan Group, Adidas, and Mazda as enterprise customers
CEO Amit Jain described Uni-1 as a model that can 'think in language and imagine and render in pixels' — what Luma calls 'intelligence in pixels'
Beta tested with over 100 clients since December 2025; API access open now with gradual rollout

stories.headline: SoftBank seeks record $40 billion loan to finance OpenAI stake
key_facts: SoftBank is seeking a bridge loan of up to $40 billion — the largest dollar-denominated corporate borrowing ever — to finance its investment in OpenAI, per Bloomberg
The bridge loan has a tenor of about 12 months, with four lenders including JPMorgan Chase underwriting the facility
SoftBank's $30 billion investment in OpenAI is part of a broader $110 billion funding round that also includes $30 billion from Nvidia and $50 billion from Amazon
SoftBank has already invested over $30 billion in OpenAI prior to this round, bringing its total commitment past $60 billion
S&P lowered SoftBank's credit outlook, citing danger that its OpenAI investments may hurt the company's liquidity and credit quality
The loan highlights founder Masayoshi Son's aggressive positioning of SoftBank as central to the AI infrastructure boom

key_facts: The UK government announced a new Fundamental AI Research Lab backed by up to £40 million over six years, plus substantial computing access worth tens of millions of pounds
Lab will target fundamental AI limitations including hallucinations, unreliable memory, and unpredictable reasoning to create more accurate and trustworthy systems
Part of the broader UKRI AI Strategy allocating £1.6 billion over four years for AI research
Peer review panel chaired by Raia Hadsell, Vice President of Research at Google DeepMind and DSIT AI Ambassador
Research areas include improving medical diagnostics, building resilient infrastructure, accelerating scientific discovery, and enhancing public service tools

stories.headline: OpenAI's GPT-5 runs 36,000 experiments in Ginkgo Bioworks autonomous lab, cuts protein costs 40%
key_facts: Ginkgo Bioworks and OpenAI demonstrated a closed-loop autonomous lab where GPT-5 designed, executed, analyzed, and refined 36,000 cell-free protein synthesis experiments over six iterative cycles
The system achieved a 40% reduction in protein production cost and 57% improvement in reagent cost versus state of the art, producing superfolder GFP at $422 per gram
GPT-5 was given internet access, a computer with data analysis packages, and experimental metadata, operating like an experimental scientist with minimal human intervention
Ginkgo's cloud laboratory in Boston uses reconfigurable automation carts (RAC) and Catalyst automation software for physical execution
The preprint was released February 5, 2026 on bioRxiv, sparking debate over whether chatbot-controlled robots could replace human biologists
Ginkgo is now commercially selling the AI-improved reaction mix in its reagents store, demonstrating commercial viability of AI-driven science

stories.headline: ICLR 2026 workshop marks recursive self-improvement's shift from theory to deployed systems
key_facts: The ICLR 2026 Workshop on AI with Recursive Self-Improvement brings together researchers to build algorithmic foundations for reliable self-improving AI systems

Workshop organizers note RSI has moved from thought experiments to deployed systems: LLM agents rewriting their own codebases, scientific discovery pipelines scheduling continual fine-tuning, and robotics stacks patching controllers from streaming telemetry
Contributions organized around five lenses: change targets inside the system, temporal regime of adaptation, mechanisms and drivers, operating contexts, and evidence of improvement
Workshop covers self-improvement across experience learning, synthetic data pipelines, multimodal agentic systems, weak-to-strong generalization, and inference-time scaling
Author notifications were sent March 1, 2026 with public release of accepted papers; workshop takes place at ICLR 2026 in Singapore
Workshop is paradigm-agnostic: welcoming work on foundation models, agent frameworks, robots, learning algorithms, optimizers, control and program synthesis

stories.headline: US drafts rules requiring permits for all Nvidia, AMD AI chip exports worldwide
key_facts: The US Commerce Department has written a 129-page draft regulation that would require government approval for virtually all exports of AI accelerators from Nvidia and AMD to any country

The proposed tiered framework sets thresholds: under 1,000 chips get streamlined review, up to 100,000 require government-to-government assurances, and 200,000+ trigger on-site US inspections and investment commitments in US AI infrastructure
A White House official stated the draft 'does not reflect what President Trump has said on export controls nor does it reflect the direction of the Trump administration'
The Commerce Department posted it will 'not' return to Biden's AI Diffusion rule, calling it 'burdensome, overreaching, and disastrous,' but did not confirm or deny the new draft
The rules would give Washington broad control over whether other countries can build AI training and inference facilities and under what conditions
Nvidia shares fell 1.9% and AMD also declined on the news

stories.headline: Pentagon places first Drone Dominance orders for 30,000 attack drones at $5,000 each
key_facts: The Department of Defense placed its first Drone Dominance program orders this week for approximately 30,000 small one-way attack drones at $5,000 per unit in Phase 1
Deliveries are slated for 17 military units beginning in March 2026, with Army and Marine units designated for live training exercises
The $1.1 billion total program targets 300,000+ domestically-produced weaponized drones by 2027, with a goal of reducing unit cost to under $2,000
25 drone companies competed in a two-week 'Gauntlet' exercise at Fort Benning, where approximately 100 service members evaluated the systems
Phase 2 testing begins in August with 50,000-60,000 additional drones and will include GPS/communications denial and electronic warfare challenges
Program manager Travis Metz said 'We asked all the military operators to evaluate whether they would take it to war, and we are buying based on those criteria'

stories.headline: BMW deploys humanoid robots at Leipzig plant, first in European auto production
key_facts: BMW launched a pilot project deploying Hexagon Robotics' AEON humanoid robot at its Leipzig plant in Germany, marking the first use of humanoid robots in European automotive production
The AEON robot, which moves on wheels, completed initial test deployment in December 2025 with a further testing phase from April 2026 and full pilot starting summer 2026
The Leipzig deployment builds on a 10-month pilot at BMW's Spartanburg USA plant where Figure 02 robots worked 10-hour shifts and supported production of over 30,000 BMW X3s
At Spartanburg, the robots handled over 90,000 components across approximately 1,250 operating hours and 1.2 million steps
BMW established a new Munich-based Center of Competence for Physical AI in Production to accelerate global integration of AI and robotics
Target tasks include high-voltage battery assembly and component manufacturing for exterior parts

stories.headline: SES activates O3b mPOWER satellites 9 and 10, reaching 10-unit operational milestone
key_facts: SES announced on March 5 that its newest pair of MEO satellites entered commercial service, bringing the O3b mPOWER fleet to 10 operational units
Satellites 9 and 10 were launched by SpaceX in July 2025 and provide terabit-level capacity with low-latency, fiber-like performance
The fully software-defined payloads built by Boeing on the 702X bus feature dynamic real-time power and bandwidth allocation
Three remaining satellites (11, 12, 13) are in final manufacturing stages with launch scheduled for the second half of 2026 to complete the 13-unit constellation
The milestone follows SES's €1.8 billion in new business wins during 2025 and the company's consolidation of Intelsat
Target applications include cruise ships, commercial aviation, military operations, and humanitarian missions

stories.headline: Waymo robotaxi blocks ambulance responding to deadly Austin mass shooting
key_facts: A Waymo autonomous vehicle obstructed ambulance crews responding to a mass shooting in downtown Austin near West 6th Street early Sunday March 3 around 2 a.m.

Footage showed the self-driving car stopped sideways across the road as an ambulance approached with flashing lights; an Austin police officer eventually entered the vehicle and drove it to a nearby garage
Waymo stated the vehicle had been hailed for pickup when it 'identified a road blockage and began executing a U-turn' before the ambulance appeared
Austin-Travis County EMS Chief Robert Luckritz said the agency was 'on scene within 57 seconds' and does not believe the incident impacted patient outcomes
The shooting killed three people and wounded 13 others; the suspect was identified as 53-year-old Ndiaga Diagne
This is the second Waymo safety incident in Austin within months, following an NTSB finding that a remote operator told a robotaxi to illegally pass a stopped school bus in January

key_facts: Generac Power Systems and EPC Power Corp announced on March 5 an engagement to deploy fully integrated energy solutions for data center applications
The systems combine Generac SBE Block battery systems and ARC Controller with EPC Power M-System inverters for behind-the-meter energy management
Solutions enable ultra-fast response times for load smoothing in AI data center applications with ride-through and recovery during grid disturbances
The integrated systems support seamless connection with onsite generators, turbines, and other resources in grid-tied or off-grid configurations
The partnership follows Generac's recent acquisition of Enercon to accelerate growth in data center and switchgear markets

stories.headline: Russia providing Iran with targeting intelligence on US warships and aircraft positions
key_facts: Russia is sharing intelligence with Iran including locations of American warships and aircraft in the Middle East, according to three US officials familiar with the intelligence
The assistance marks the first indication that another major US adversary is participating, even indirectly, in the Iran war
Iran's own ability to locate US forces has been degraded since the US and Israel launched strikes against Tehran on February 28
Russian intelligence may include satellite imagery and data helping Iran target American military infrastructure including command centers and radar installations
The White House did not directly comment on the alleged Russian support, with spokeswoman Anna Kelly stating Iran's capabilities are 'being absolutely crushed'
NBC News reported there is no indication Moscow is helping direct Iranian missile or drone strikes, but the data could help Iran locate warships, radar, or communication systems

stories.headline: House narrowly rejects Iran war powers resolution 212-219, second congressional defeat in two days
key_facts: The US House voted 212-219 to reject a war powers resolution that would have curbed President Trump's authority to continue military operations against Iran
The vote follows the Senate's 53-47 defeat of a similar measure the previous day
House Speaker Mike Johnson called it 'dangerous' to limit the president's authority while the military is already in conflict
Rep. Gregory Meeks, top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said 'Donald Trump is not a king' and must come to Congress to make the case for war
The narrow margin reflected unease among some Republicans, with the conflict drawing echoes of the long wars in Afghanistan and Iraq
Johnson contradicted himself by saying 'We are not at war' while arguing for wartime presidential authority

key_facts: Trump posted on Truth Social: 'There will be no deal with Iran except UNCONDITIONAL SURRENDER!' on the war's seventh day
Trump said after surrender, the US would help select 'a GREAT & ACCEPTABLE Leader(s)' and work to 'MAKE IRAN GREAT AGAIN (MIGA!)'
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told NBC that Iran is 'not asking for a ceasefire' and is ready for any US ground invasion
Trump told NBC News a ground invasion would be a 'waste of time'
Israeli military announced a 'broad wave' of strikes on Tehran targeting regime infrastructure, with approximately 50 jets striking Khamenei's underground bunker
IDF said it destroyed the underground bunker beneath Khamenei's residence that was being used by senior military officials after his killing on February 28
More than 1,300 people have been killed in Iran since the war began, according to the Iranian Red Crescent

stories.headline: US economy unexpectedly shed 92,000 jobs in February as unemployment rises to 4.4%
key_facts: US employers cut 92,000 jobs in February, far below economists' forecast of 55,000-60,000 new jobs
Unemployment rate rose to 4.4% from 4.3% in January
Prior months revised down by a combined 69,000 jobs from December and January payrolls
Labor force participation fell to 62.0%, the lowest since December 2021
Health care, professional and business services, and financial activities saw positive job growth while retail trade and leisure and hospitality drove losses
Stocks tumbled after the report, with Dow futures losing more than 600 points as traders also weighed Iran war developments and oil prices near $90/barrel
January payrolls were revised from 130,000 to 126,000 added jobs

key_facts: Brent crude surged past $90 per barrel on March 6, its highest price since 2023, driven by the escalating Iran war
US benchmark WTI crude jumped 8.5% on Thursday to settle at $81.01, then continued rising Friday
The S&P 500 fell 1% on Friday, erasing its year-to-date gains, heading for its worst week since November
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped more than 900 points on Friday after the weak jobs report compounded oil fears
Average US gasoline prices rose 9% in one week to $3.25 per gallon from $2.98
Markets faced a dual shock of rising oil prices and weak employment data, raising fears of stagflation with no easy central bank fix
Dow had already dropped 784 points on Thursday after oil spiked to its highest since summer 2024

stories.headline: Nature Aging: glycolytic metabolite PEP identified as natural anti-aging mechanism that inhibits inflammation
key_facts: A study published in Nature Aging on March 6 shows phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), a glycolytic metabolite, acts as a protective factor against age-related chronic inflammation
PEP works by competitively binding to cGAS, inhibiting the cGAS-STING inflammatory pathway that drives inflammaging
Longitudinal analyses in mice and humans reveal a biphasic PEP trajectory: initial accumulation during aging followed by progressive decline
Administering PEP before its natural decline promoted healthy aging in mice; blocking PEP accumulation accelerated aging phenotypes
In aged humans, high PEP levels strongly correlate with lower inflammation and healthier traits
PEP also alleviated neuroinflammation and improved cognitive function in an Alzheimer's disease mouse model
The findings position PEP as a promising intervention target for aging and age-related diseases including neurodegeneration

stories.headline: Buck Institute launches Healthspan Horizons to link wearable data with aging biology research
key_facts: The Buck Institute for Research on Aging announced Healthspan Horizons, a federated data initiative to measure, understand, and extend healthspan
The platform links real-world longitudinal data from wearables, sleep, activity, nutrition, and labs with deep biological measurements
The initiative aims to detect disease decades before clinical diagnosis by identifying early biological shifts
Healthspan Horizons uses responsible AI and federated data architecture to combine heterogeneous multimodal datasets
The project addresses the gap where people live longer but spend added years managing chronic disease rather than in good health
The Buck Institute is a California-based research institute dedicated to aging research

An AWS facility in Bahrain was also damaged by a nearby drone strike
Iranian state media said the Bahrain facility was targeted for Amazon's support of the US military
The strikes represent a new category of military targets as data centers become strategic infrastructure in modern warfare
